daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo Subianto conducted field inspections of forest and land fires in Kalimantan, visiting West and Central Kalimantan to assess the firefighting response. During the visit, Prabowo vowed action against firms linked to the fires and ordered an immediate halt to the spread of fire hotspots. The president also announced plans to deploy an additional 1,500 TNI personnel and additional helicopters to combat the fires.

  • State Secretary revealed that four corporations are under investigation for their potential role in the West Kalimantan fires, with the government insisting violators must be prosecuted if evidence is found.
  • Home Minister Tito Karnavian accompanied President Prabowo during the West Kalimantan inspection and then traveled to Central Kalimantan to discuss strengthening firefighting operations.
  • A DPR member from Golkar urged BMKG to strengthen its earthquake early warning system following recent seismic activity.
  • An opposition DPR member called for universities to be free from corruption following the KPK detention of the Unsoed rector.
  • Hanura party changed its symbol to a lion in preparation for the 2029 elections.
  • PSI's daily chairman Ahmad Ali denied accusations of jumping the gun on 2029 election campaigning, saying PSI started early intentionally.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo Subianto hosted Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Defence Minister Dong Jun to deepen bilateral ties between Jakarta and Beijing. During the meetings, Indonesia and China agreed to deepen cooperation in digital technology and artificial intelligence. Foreign Minister Wang Yi separately met with Luhut Panjaitan to discuss investment matters.

  • China's Defence Minister pushed for enhanced defence cooperation with Indonesia during his visit to Jakarta.
  • Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi highlighted the importance of Indonesia's position in regional diplomacy.
  • Indonesia and Turkey jointly condemned Israeli attacks on a Syrian military base.
  • Indonesia and seven Arab nations criticized the expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
  • Indonesia's embassy in Bern supported a partnership between Kadin and Suissenegoce to train trade human resources.

Other

Relief efforts continued for earthquake survivors in East Nusa Tenggara, with the disaster displacing 150,576 people as the death toll rose to 87. The Indonesian Red Cross dispatched 33,947 relief items while the government airlifted 777 tons of aid and pledged continued support until full recovery.

  • The Communications Ministry confirmed that 812 mobile base stations affected by the NTT earthquake have been restored to service.
  • Firefighters are battling a spreading wildfire in Way Kambas National Park, while the government deployed eight aircraft and 1,500 troops with six helicopters to combat forest fires across Kalimantan.
  • BMKG urged fire mitigation measures as East Kalimantan recorded 11,869 fire hotspots.
  • The KPK seized Rp 665 million in cash and Rp 99 million in bank account balances during the operation that detained the Unsoed rector, and explained why the Vice Rector II was not named a suspect despite being caught in the sting.
  • The government targets early 2027 for implementation of the IEU-CEPA trade agreement, now in final stages.
